pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How should you find out how your mother tongue forms plurals? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   B. Guess from English
   C. Ignore it
   D. Add s to every word

2. Why do we keep a class portfolio of songs? (1 mark)
   A. So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   B. To hide them
   C. To sell them
   D. To throw them away

3. What is the plural of the English word mango? (1 mark)
   A. mangoss
   B. mangos'
   C. mangoies
   D. mangoes

4. Vocabulary means (1 mark)
   A. only names
   B. only long words
   C. all the words you know and can use
   D. the pictures in a book

5. What is a good way to give feedback to a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Say nothing
   B. Say they are bad
   C. Laugh at mistakes
   D. Say one good thing and one thing to improve

6. Why should instructions be clear? (1 mark)
   A. So nobody listens
   B. So they are longer
   C. So people are confused
   D. So the listener can do the right thing

7. What should listeners do after a group reads aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at the readers
   B. Tear the script
   C. Give kind and helpful feedback
   D. Leave the room

8. What does a full stop show? (1 mark)
   A. A sudden feeling
   B. The end of a statement
   C. A list of items
   D. A question

9. What should you keep the same in a paragraph unless there is a reason to change? (1 mark)
   A. The page
   B. The pen
   C. The time of the verbs
   D. The paper colour

10. What is a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. One word
   B. A title
   C. A group of sentences about one main idea
   D. A page number

11. Which comma use is correct? (1 mark)
   A. When the bell, rang we ran.
   B. When the bell rang we, ran.
   C. When, the bell rang we ran.
   D. When the bell rang, we ran.

12. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A list
   C. A short play
   D. A long poem

13. Which sentence joins two events with when? (1 mark)
   A. I smiled the gift.
   B. When the gift.
   C. Saw I gift.
   D. I smiled when I saw the gift.

14. Which is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Table
   B. Quickly
   C. Beside
   D. Hurray!

15. What is a talent? (1 mark)
   A. A book
   B. A skill you are good at
   C. A kind of food
   D. A rule

16. Why should you not invent interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. They are learned from speakers of the language
   B. Nobody uses them
   C. Languages have no interjections
   D. It is easy to invent them correctly

17. What are notes? (1 mark)
   A. Short records of important points
   B. Songs
   C. Pictures only
   D. Long stories

18. What does an interjection show? (1 mark)
   A. A number
   B. A sudden feeling
   C. A time
   D. A place

19. Which punctuation mark often follows an interjection showing strong feeling? (1 mark)
   A. Colon
   B. Exclamation mark
   C. Full stop
   D. Question mark

20. How should you start a new speaker's words in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Inside a bracket
   B. On a new line
   C. On the same line as before
   D. At the end of the page

21. Which is a difference between an advert and a news item? (1 mark)
   A. Adverts report elections only
   B. News is always a poem
   C. They are exactly the same
   D. An advert tries to sell and news reports facts

22. What does N/A mean? (1 mark)
   A. New address
   B. No answer always
   C. Next assignment
   D. Not applicable

23. What should you do after filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Give it to anyone
   B. Check it and sign and date it
   C. Ignore it
   D. Throw it away

24. What should you use to fill a form unless told otherwise? (1 mark)
   A. A chalk
   B. A pen
   C. A crayon
   D. A finger

25. What should a real-life experience description include? (1 mark)
   A. Only a number
   B. Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   C. Only a title
   D. Nothing

26. What is a good leader described as in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. Rude
   B. Lazy
   C. Angry
   D. Fair and kind

27. What is a poem's title? (1 mark)
   A. Its last line
   B. Its name
   C. Its page
   D. Its rhyme

28. What is a choral poem? (1 mark)
   A. A written test
   B. A silent poem
   C. A poem performed by a group together
   D. A map

29. What should you add when a task is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. A colour
   B. A joke
   C. A song
   D. A warning

30. Which is a verb in Open your book? (1 mark)
   A. Open
   B. book
   C. your
   D. the

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write a five-sentence oral paragraph about a free day. Include three interjections that show different feelings. (5 marks)

32. Write a short speech of four sentences about caring for a goat. Use at least two prepositions. (5 marks)

33. Write the verbs in this instruction: Open your book and read page ten. (2 marks)

34. Write four numbered steps for crossing a road safely. (4 marks)

35. Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally. (4 marks)

36. Explain what a form is. (2 marks)

37. Give three questions to ask when reading an advert. (3 marks)

38. Give three qualities of a good leader mentioned in the model poem lead with honesty. (3 marks)

39. Write one correct line of a dialogue with a speaker name and an interjection. (2 marks)

40. Explain why clear instructions are important on a road. (3 marks)

41. Describe what a written dialogue shows. (2 marks)

42. Copy this sentence correctly: the food is hot (2 marks)

43. Explain the difference in punctuation between Wow! and Oops, it is torn. (3 marks)

44. Compose a short poem of four lines about caring for animals. Make two lines rhyme. (5 marks)

45. Give three good manners to show when collecting proverbs from an elder. (3 marks)

46. Give two rules for looking after class library books. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   Languages form plurals in different ways, so we ask people who know the language well.

2. A — So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   A portfolio preserves the songs collected from the community.

3. D — mangoes
   Mango takes es in the plural, mangoes.

4. C — all the words you know and can use
   Vocabulary is a person's collection of words.

5. D — Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   Kind and useful feedback helps people improve.

6. D — So the listener can do the right thing
   Clear instructions prevent mistakes.

7. C — Give kind and helpful feedback
   Feedback helps readers improve.

8. B — The end of a statement
   A full stop ends a statement.

9. C — The time of the verbs
   Keep past, present or future consistent.

10. C — A group of sentences about one main idea
   A paragraph has one main idea.

11. D — When the bell rang, we ran.
   A comma follows the when part at the start.

12. C — A short play
   A skit is a short acted scene.

13. D — I smiled when I saw the gift.
   It uses when to link two events.

14. D — Hurray!
   Hurray shows joy.

15. B — A skill you are good at
   A talent is a natural ability.

16. A — They are learned from speakers of the language
   Ask real speakers for correct forms.

17. A — Short records of important points
   Notes are brief points.

18. B — A sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotions.

19. B — Exclamation mark
   Exclamation marks show strong feeling.

20. B — On a new line
   A new line shows a new speaker.

21. D — An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   Their purposes differ.

22. D — Not applicable
   N/A means the question does not apply.

23. B — Check it and sign and date it
   Checking prevents mistakes.

24. B — A pen
   A pen gives clear permanent writing.

25. B — Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   These details make it clear.

26. D — Fair and kind
   The poem advises fairness and kindness.

27. B — Its name
   The title names the poem.

28. C — A poem performed by a group together
   Chorus means together.

29. D — A warning
   Warnings keep people safe.

30. A — Open
   Open is the action.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five sentences with three suitable interjections such as Hurray, Wow and Oops used to show joy, surprise and a mistake.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for three suitable interjections shown correctly.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two prepositions, for example Give the goat water beside the food. Build a shed behind the house. Do not put a heavy load on it. Call the veterinary doctor if it is sick.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for correct prepositions.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: open, read
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1. Stop at the edge. 2. Look right, left and right. 3. Listen for vehicles. 4. Cross when the road is clear.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in a sensible order.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form is a page with spaces where people write information in an organised way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a page with spaces and one for collecting information.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: What is being sold, who is it for, what is the price, where can I get it, is it as good as it says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fair, true, listens, shares the work, kind, strong (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema: Wow! The sun is shining.
   Working / marking points: One mark for name with colon and one for an interjection.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear road instructions and signs tell drivers and walkers what to do, which prevents accidents and keeps everyone safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for telling what to do, one for preventing accidents, one for safety.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people written to show what each speaker says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for showing speakers' words.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The food is hot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the capital letter and one mark for the full stop.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma after a mild interjection shows a softer feeling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each punctuation mark and one for the difference.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on the theme with a pair of rhyming lines, for example Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play, Kind hands keep her safe and well, That is how we care, we tell.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme, two marks for four lines and one mark for a rhyming pair.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet politely, listen without interrupting, ask permission to write, say thank you.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Turn pages gently, never write in them, return them on time, keep them clean (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.
